clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute hemorrhagic oedema of infancy (AHEI), also known as Finkelstein-Seidlmayer disease
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-month-old girl presented with petechiae on the soft palate 12 days post-MMR vaccination and 8 days after febrile diarrhea, with subsequent progressive hemorrhagic rash extending to the skin. Initial workup excluded immune thrombocytopenic purpura with normal platelet counts (171,000-180,000/mm3). Physical examination revealed petechial-hemorrhagic lesions with sharp merges on the limbs, face, and auricles with prominent edema. During hospitalization, bilateral metacarpophalangeal joint edema with pain developed on day 2 but responded to paracetamol and resolved within one week. Comprehensive laboratory evaluation including coagulation studies, renal function, and inflammatory markers was performed. Abdominal and urinary tract ultrasound excluded visceral involvement. The skin manifestations spontaneously resolved within 3 weeks without sequelae, consistent with the characteristic benign, self-limited course of AHEI.
